title: Torque Limiter
model_title: Friction Torque Limiter (Slip Clutch) with Chain Sprocket

introduction.definition: A torque limiter protects a drive from overload. In a friction type, disc springs clamp the driven member (sprocket) between friction facings; below the set torque it drives normally, above it the facings slip and the jam does not damage motor or gearbox.

classification.type: Friction slip clutch with chain sprocket

introduction.summary: A torque limiter protects machines from overload. In this friction type, disc springs clamp a sprocket between friction facings on a hub. Up to the set torque everything turns together; if the driven machine jams, the facings slip so the motor and gearbox are not damaged. The slip torque is set by tightening the adjusting nut.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Transmitted torque rises with load until the slip torque, then stays roughly constant while slipping.

torque.title: Driving torque vs load torque
torque.description: Disc springs clamp the sprocket between the friction facings. While the load torque (red) is below the set slip torque, the friction transmits the drive torque (magenta) and everything turns together. On a jam the load torque exceeds the setting: the facings slip, the hub keeps turning and the sprocket stops — protecting the drive. Tighten the nut to raise the setting.

foundation: Mount driver and driven machines on a rigid common base so centre distances and alignment stay fixed.
alignment: Align shafts parallel and the wheels/hubs in the same plane (straight-edge or laser); misalignment is the main cause of early wear.
piping: Fit guards that fully enclose moving parts but allow inspection and lubrication.
commissioning: Set the nut to the maker's chart for the required slip torque; run in the facings; verify slip with a torque wrench.

routine.task: Check for signs of slipping (heat, dust).

lubrication: No lubrication of facings; grease the sprocket bush only if specified.

video_tutorials.title: Torque Limiter — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Torque Limiter.
A torque limiter protects a drive from overload.

In a friction type, disc springs clamp the driven member (sprocket) between friction facings; below the set torque it drives normally, above it the facings slip and the jam does not damage motor or gearbox.
Typical applications include conveyors and feeders; packaging and printing machines; crushers and mixers; agricultural machinery.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Hub on Driving Shaft (with marker), Sprocket (driven member, free on a bush) — stops on overload.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Torque Limiter — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Torque Limiter.
Check for signs of slipping (heat, dust).
Verify slip torque.
Replace facings and bush.
Watch for nuisance slipping: slips under normal load. Common cause: setting too low, worn/oily facings.
Watch for no slip on jam: damage to drive. Common cause: rusted/seized facings, over-tightened.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
